Banzai Escape is a port of the Android rail shooter of the same name. Given its origins as a mobile game, the graphics are about what you would expect, which is to say not very good. Strangely enough some parts of the game seem to suffer from performance issues as well, which is not something you would expect from a game designed to run on a phone. In a rarity for a mobile port, the game actually features graphical options like resolution, fullscreen or windowed play, shadow detail, and anti-aliasing, which was a pleasant surprise.

The game suffers from fairly significant input lag, to the point that it can take multiple seconds to force the character to reload or pop in or out of cover, which can quickly prove fatal. I would not describe the game as difficult per se, though I agree with the game's description in that you will die a lot. The game is about 90% memorization and 10% skill. An example occurs in the first level when an enemy charges you with a knife. You have just a few seconds to shoot him before he moves outside of the area you can aim at, at which point he kills you instantly.

Banzai Escape features a swap cover feature, but there is no indication of where or when you can swap cover. More than once the cover you will swap to is not even visible on screen. You can only press the swap cover button on each screen and see what happens. The game also fails to mention that even behind cover, you can be killed while blind firing or reloading. I'll accept the blind firing part as you are exposing part of your body to shoot, but you are still entirely behind cover when reloading. In one early level, you can be killed even while behind cover and neither blind firing or reloading.

Expect to grind a lot. You will need money to purchase new weapons and increase your ammunition capacity, which will have you playing the same few levels many times.

The writing and the voice acting are not very well done, though the game does deserve some praise for featuring English voice acting in addition to the written dialogue. The translation is perfectly serviceable, I had no difficulty understanding what was going on.

As mobile ports go, this one was handled pretty well. However the game itself is frustrating and generally not a lot of fun to play. If you do choose to pick the game up, I would recommend waiting until it goes on sale.

Tried to play this. Really tried hard. Simple rail shooter that is definitely better than Rambo: the video game.

Too bad it fails it's own gameplay mechanics.

The Good:

- Voice acting is pretty good for a low cost game. Well done.

- Rail shooter gameplay is pretty good.

- I like it how you include skins and weapon options into the game. And for FREE (looking at you EA games! <XD)

The average:

- English subtitles could use Google Translate. Or someone who speaks, reads and writes English well.

- Controls seem average. Apparently the forth mission is bollocks though.

The Bad:

- States that if you stick out of cover or behind cover you can be hit. Simply put you can just sit still and be hit anyway. This shouldn't happen and the developer even insists that it does not.

- Before the third misson you are told you need better gear. You are given the options to purchase a FAMAS. Too bad you don't have enough money to buy it and supply it with a LOT of ammo.

- In the tutorial you are told that a white glowing light means it is invicible. A blue glowing light means you can attack it and so forth. Against the third boss I copuld only use my Glock pistol to engage the boss. Blue l;ight being hit state 'Resist". Should include this information in the tutorial! I honestly did not know if the game was bugged or I was being stupid. Turns out your glock is useless against bosses.

- Playing the same mission over, and over, and over again to earn money to buy ammo to use a good gun in order to complete the mission is not a good gameplay mechanic.

Conclusion:

Good title for it's price. It's not Great! but at the same time it's not Terrible. Still in it's final release I cannot reccommend it as it will cost you money and I gave up on the third mission. Only because I had to play it over, and over, and over again just to get money to buy ammo to complete it. Pretty much a 4/10.
